answer.line: Only first order has a half-life with no starting concentration in it, so only first order keeps it constant.

steps: Know the three half-lives. Zero order: [A]_0 / 2k. First order: 0.693 / k. Second order: 1 / (k[A]_0).
Look for [A]_0. Only the first-order form leaves it out, so only first order gives the same half-life from any start.
Picture the decay: zero order's halvings come faster, second order's come slower, first order's come evenly spaced.

choices.note: Second-order half-life is 1 / (k[A]_0). As the concentration falls, each half-life gets longer.
Third order slows even more as [A] falls, so each half-life is longer than the last.
At half order the half-life shrinks as [A] falls, more gently than zero order. It still depends on the start.
Zero order runs at a constant rate, which tempts you here. Its half-life is [A]_0 / 2k, so each halving comes sooner.

lockIt: A half-life that ignores the starting concentration means first order.
